page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-1xCPU-4GB is a general-purpose, entry-tier virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 1 shared x86_64 vCPU derived from an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 4.0 GB of system memory. Hardware features include 16 MB of L3 cache, standard hardware virtualization, and CPU instruction sets such as AVX, AES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes no bundled local storage and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring attached network storage volumes and external networking configurations for standard deployment scenarios.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-thread burst potential alongside the throughput boundaries expected of a single shared core. In Geekbench testing, the server attained a single-core score of 2295.0, reflecting modern EPYC microarchitecture efficiency. However, aggregate processing capacity remains limited, with a multi-core score of 2225.0, a PassMark CPU score of 2027.8, and single/multi-core stress-ng results of 737.38. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth measures 9.03 GB/sec for reads and 7.89 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, the node achieved 1.36 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.1 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given its single shared-core allocation and 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, CLOUDNATIVE-1xCPU-4GB delivers resource-dense, low-cost utility for non-intensive compute tiers. It is well suited for lightweight microservices, testing and staging environments, low-traffic web endpoints, background workers, and containerized utilities that benefit from 4 GB of memory without requiring sustained multi-core compute.
